conventions.plane_basis: B = Rz(rz) * Rx(rx) * Ry(ry); world = origin + B * local; local Y is the plane normal
conventions.view_frame: with a pinned plane every viewport read (focus, orientation, pixel->point) is in plane-local coordinates; an orthographic view is re-expressed in the plane's frame, so it turns with the plane

laws.placement: the gesture point is computed in PLANE-LOCAL view coordinates (ray through the pixel, meeting the local principal plane whose axis is the largest component of the local view direction, through the grid-rounded local camera focus) and written to the channels; world = origin + B * channels. The primitive therefore lies on the ray of the pixel it was placed at (cylinder/sphere: the press pixel = centre; box: the release pixel = centre, press = corner). d_perp <= snap quantum in every cell.
laws.motionless_click: writes the channels, size 0, and creates no geometry
laws.orientation: the primitive is axis-aligned in the plane frame (typed oblique plane, two non-zero angles)

skew_edge_pair.applies_when: exactly two edges selected that share no endpoint and no polygon (an adjacent pair or a pair on one polygon takes other, already recorded, paths)
skew_edge_pair.origin: bounding-box centre of the selected edges' endpoints
skew_edge_pair.normal_y: least-squares plane n . p = 1 through the endpoint positions p (world): n = (sum p p^T)^-1 (sum p); flipped so mean(p) . n >= 0; normalised; then flipped so its largest-magnitude component is positive. NOT translation-invariant: the fit is anchored at the world origin (singular when every point lies on a plane through the world origin -- not exercised)
roll: k = index of the largest-magnitude component of the normal; M = the shortest-arc rotation taking the normal onto the unit axis e_k; 2-D coordinates (u, v) = ((M p)[a1], (M p)[a2]) with (a1, a2) = ((1,2), (2,0), (0,1))[k]
convex hull of the 2-D points (start = lowest v, ties highest u; counter-clockwise; collinear nearer points dropped)

major direction: the first strictly farthest pair of hull points (i < j), flipped so v >= 0, scored by length x width; then the four hull edges adjacent to that pair (i-1,i), (i,i+1), (j-1,j), (j,j+1) each give an edge-aligned bounding rectangle whose direction is its longer side (flipped so v >= 0); a candidate replaces the current one only if its area is STRICTLY smaller
tie branch (length == width): square bbox equal to that length -> direction (0, 1); else swap the components when |du| > |dv| (not exercised)
3-D direction d = M^T (du e_a1 + dv e_a2)
skew_edge_pair.axes: Y = normal; X = normalize(Y x d); Z = X x Y (= d); rows (X, Y, Z) give the plane rotation in the B = Rz Rx Ry convention
skew_edge_pair.measured: reproduces a-2e-skew and a-2e-skew-t (matrix residual <= 5e-15) and four new rigs within 0.0005 deg

mixed_group_control.note: same drive with the startup projections left by the worker bootstrap: the orthographic link group then contained a perspective-projected cell; that group kept its WORLD focus across the pin (local = B^T(W - O), residual < 1e-4)

cells.law: cells share a focus by their LINK GROUP, not by projection: the three orthographic cells share one focus, the perspective cell has its own (a pan in either never moves the other). When a plane is pinned the orthographic group keeps its plane-LOCAL focus numbers (its world focus jumps to O + B*nums, as a single orthographic cell does) and its views turn with the plane; the perspective cell keeps its WORLD focus. A group that contains a perspective-projected cell keeps its world focus instead

laws.focus_on_plane_change_ortho: the focus NUMBERS are kept across align, typed pin and reset (local after = world before, and back): the world focus jumps to origin + B * numbers. Rival 'world focus kept' predicted (0.3, -0.5, -0.2) after the face-0 align and reads (0.3, 0.2, 0)
laws.ortho_presets_turn: front, top and right all turn with the plane: after the change the plane-local orientation rows equal the canonical preset rows
laws.typed_plane_turns_ortho: a TYPED oblique plane turns the front view too (the model is then drawn obliquely)
laws.perspective_keeps_world_camera: control: world orientation rows and world eye are unchanged by the align; the local focus reads B^T(world focus - origin)
laws.focus_write_after_pin_is_local: a focus written while a plane is pinned is plane-local; a capture that pins first and then sets the focus exercised no plane-change transition
laws.focus_pinned_to_pinned: pinned to pinned (re-align to another face): the focus NUMBERS are kept again, so the world focus jumps from origin + B * numbers to origin' + B' * numbers ((0.3, 0, 0.7) -> (0, 0.7, 0.3) here); the front view turns into the new plane (canonical front rows). 'World focus kept' predicted local (0.7, -0.5, -0.3), 0.86 away; 'reset to the new origin' predicted (0, 0, 0), 0.36 away
